title_ar: استشفاء الشيخ الددو لفضيلة الشيخ العلامة محمد محمود أحمد يورة الرباني
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew's Prayer for the Recovery of His Eminence the Learned Sheikh Muhammad Mahmud Ahmad Yura al-Rabbani
body_ar:
يا ربنا اشف شيخنا محمدا

محمودا الجائز في الفضل المدى

سلسل أحمد يورة من تفردا

في العلم والخلق فكان الأوحدا

أنور وجها وأجل محتدا

أصدق لهجة وأكرم يدا

أحسن سيرة وأعلى سندا

أطهر قلبا وأدق مقصدا

قد شاد مجدا للأبين أتلدا

في حلة الجود أئمة الهدى

رب أنله المبتغى والمقصدا

وأبقه وانصره نصرا أيدا

وفي البنين أبق ما تعودا

يقفون ذاك سيدا فسيدا

و أعط مريم مناها المسعدا

و استجب الدعاء و اكبت العدى
body_en:
O our Lord, heal our sheikh Muhammad

Mahmud, who has traversed the farthest reach in excellence,

of the line of Ahmad Yura, who stood alone

in knowledge and in character, and so was without peer,

the most radiant of face and the most noble of descent,

the most truthful in speech and the most open-handed,

the finest in conduct and the highest in chain of transmission,

the purest of heart and the most exacting in purpose.

He has built a glory for the two forefathers, long inherited,

clothed in generosity, the imams of guidance.

Lord, grant him what he seeks and what he aims at,

preserve him and help him with a strengthening help,

and in his sons let what has been customary continue,

that they stand, one master after another.

Grant Maryam the wish that will make her happy,

answer this supplication, and subdue the enemies.

options: who has traversed the farthest reach in excellence
who has crossed the whole span of excellence
to whom the utmost degree of excellence is granted
flags.note: CRITICAL FALSE FRIEND. الجائز here is the active participle of جاز, 'to traverse or cross', in praise of the sheikh's attainment. It is NOT the legal jāʾiz, 'permissible', of style guide section 3, nor the kalām jāʾiz, 'rationally possible', of section 8. Applying either mapping would make nonsense of the line. Flagged so that no automated glossary pass converts it.

flags.context: the third line of the poem
options: of the line of Ahmad Yura, who stood alone
descendant of Ahmad Yura, the one who was unique
a link in the chain of Ahmad Yura, who had no equal
flags.note: سلسل is not the ordinary سليل ('scion') or سلسلة ('chain'); the form is unusual and may be metrical licence, a Mauritanian usage, or a CMS typo. The sense 'of the line/chain of' fits both the genealogy and the isnād reading of the next lines, but the choice affects whether the poem is praising descent or scholarly transmission.

flags.context: the ninth line of the poem
options: He has built a glory for the two forefathers, long inherited
He has raised for the two ancestral lines a glory of ancient standing
He has built an inherited glory for both his forebears
flags.note: للأبين is dual, 'the two fathers', most likely the paternal and maternal lines, but it could be two named ancestors known to the family. أتلد is 'most long-inherited'. The referent cannot be fixed from the text and needs the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: the fifteenth line of the poem
options: Grant Maryam the wish that will make her happy
flags.note: Maryam is named without further identification; presumably a member of the sheikh's household. Kept as a personal name with no gloss added.

translator_notes: Verse (nazm). Style guide section 4 requires verse to be rendered as prose in italics with the Arabic retained in the bilingual pane; body_ar carries the Arabic line for line and body_en keeps the same line division so the two panes align. No rhymed English has been attempted.

Genre: a supplication in verse for a scholar's recovery, filed by the site under الشعر (Poetry). The schema's type list has no value for poetry, so 'article' has been used; the genre is recorded here and in section/category. The schema should gain a poetry type.
استشفاء is seeking a cure for someone, here by supplication; 'prayer for the recovery of' is used rather than the medical 'seeking treatment'.
No ruling of any kind is given, so the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged.

The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload/publication stamp, not the date on which the Sheikh gave the answer. Records across this range carry timestamps clustered minutes apart on the same day (e.g. 1275-1278 at 09:51/09:53/09:54/09:55 on 7 March 2022), which is the signature of a batch upload. date_is_cms_upload is therefore set true throughout.
